candidate_slices.why: Some already-reviewed non-refusal groups have strong evidence, but expanding beyond those groups needs exact branch inventory first.
candidate_slices.risk: Could duplicate already-promoted safe-call-control behavior or accidentally widen approved branches.

candidate_slices.why: Some localized responses may exist without classifier reachability; inventory can separate dead responses from intentionally blocked routes.
candidate_slices.risk: Making dormant responses reachable without review can surface unapproved wording.

candidate_slices.why: Unknown turns are currently safest as clarification. Splitting unknowns requires evidence that a subtype has a safer deterministic route.
candidate_slices.risk: Over-classification could reduce clarification and force wrong branches.

candidate_slices.why: Any classifier expansion must prove it does not swallow support, do-not-call, payment, healthcare, coverage, voicemail, human-request, or email-only boundaries.
candidate_slices.risk: False positives in protected boundaries are higher severity than missed sales opportunities.

inventory_requirements: separate already-approved selected non-refusal groups from unreviewed branches
attach protected-boundary controls to every candidate slice
recommend at most one narrow probe as the next runtime-adjacent step
